findings.title: Unchecked property access on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is empty or null
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` as `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`. On line 119, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining (`?.`). Any booking with `location === MeetLocationType` (`integrations:google:meet`) and no destination calendar configured will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back to `integrations:daily`.

findings.title: Co-host destinationCalendars are silently dropped when the organizer has no destinationCalendar
findings.body: On lines 1063-1067, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining, which is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. As a result, in a collective event where the main organizer has no destination calendar set on their account/event type, all other hosts' destination calendars in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded and their calendar events are never created.

findings.title: `calendar.events.patch` for Meet link uses `undefined` calendarId instead of falling back to `"primary"`
findings.body: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` was previously defaulted to `"primary"` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId ? ... : "primary"`). Now `selectedCalendar` is `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which can be `undefined` (for example, when `destination.credentialId` is not set or no entry matches). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call on line 168 passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly without `|| "primary"`, causing the patch that adds the Google Meet hangout link to the event description to fail.

findings.title: Fallback lookup in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compares `cal.externalId` against falsy `externalCalendarId`
findings.body: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of the ternary `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`). Searching for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` in that branch can therefore never match a valid calendar `externalId` and will always evaluate to `undefined` (replacing the previous fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). In `updateEvent`, this passes `calendarId: undefined` to `calendar.events.update`.

findings.title: Removed `organization` selection from `loadUsers` breaks organization slug resolution for dynamic bookings
findings.body: In `loadUsers` (lines 735-739), `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` was removed from the `prisma.user.findMany` select clause when `!eventTypeId` (dynamic group bookings). The inferred return type of `loadUsers` and downstream code that accesses `user.organization.slug` on dynamic booking users will no longer have `organization` loaded.

findings.title: Unrelated change in organization `createHandler` inverts `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` slug logic
findings.body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts` line 151, `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. When team billing is enabled, the slug is supposed to be held in `metadata.requestedSlug` (line 153) until billing is completed, and only set directly on `slug` when billing is disabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). Flipping this condition sets `slug` immediately when billing is enabled and leaves `slug` unset when billing is disabled, breaking self-hosted/non-billed organization creation and bypassing the billing gate on billed instances.
